newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl appeals for reason on reduced sick-pay.
newsitem.headline: Kohl appeals for reason on reduced sick-pay.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Monday appealed to labour and employers to avoid an escalation of tensions over reduced sick pay compensation.
Reductions in sick pay passed by the government as part of its Programme for More Jobs and Growth do not mean that existing contracts are no longer valid, Kohl said.
"It is up to the wage negotiating parties to find acceptable solutions within the new framework," Kohl said in a statement. "A sharpening of the conflict would be economically damaging."
Kohl said the new rules would bring Germany into line with practices in other countries and ease the burden on employers.
The laws, introduced earlier this month, allow employers to pay 80 percent compensation for sick days rather than the previous 100 percent. Sick pay in Germany now totals 60 billion marks a year.
Some employers have already canceled contracts and said they aim to move immediately to the reduced sick pay.
The IG Metall union has called labour actions on October 10 to protest the move.
